lessons.title: Looking for the Furry Cat

activities.prompt: Where might the furry cat be hiding?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: Follow the Cat Clues
activities.body: This poem is a playful hunt for the furry cat. It tells you to keep looking and asks about the window, the bed, the red rack and the backpack. It also gives clues from a jar, a car, a mat and a hat. Top means high, while bottom means low. Below means under, and above means over. At last, the poem says that the furry cat has come.
keyPoints: Keep looking for the furry cat.
The poem gives clues about many places.
At last, the furry cat has come.
activities.explanation: The poem moves through cat clues until the furry cat appears.

activities.prompt: The poem says the cat was scratching the bottom of the jar. A child hears a scratching sound there. Where might the furry cat have been?
steps: The poem says the cat was scratching the bottom of the jar.
The sound is at the bottom of the jar, so it matches that action.
Therefore, the furry cat may have been at the jar.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.prompt: The poem asks if the cat is sleeping under the bed.
activities.explanation: Yes. The poem asks if the cat is sleeping under the bed.

activities.hint: This is a bag that you can carry.
activities.explanation: The poem asks if the cat is inside the backpack.

activities.prompt: Match each place with its cat clue.
activities.explanation: Each place matches the action or position asked about in the poem.

above the hat

below the mat

activities.title: Above or Below?
activities.prompt: The poem says the cat was hopping below the mat.
activities.explanation: The cat was hopping above the hat. It was hiding below the mat.

lessons.title: Looking, Hiding and Finding

activities.prompt: Where is the ball hiding, and how can we help it find its way?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: Look, Describe and Find
activities.body: Look carefully at each picture. You can talk about what you see and where things are. Words such as above, below, on and under help you describe positions. The book uses cats, dogs and cows in questions about position. You can hide things, give directions and throw a ball into a basket. Inside and outside tell you what happens to the ball.
keyPoints: Look carefully and tell what you see.
Use words to describe where things are.
Say IN or OUT when the ball goes in or out.
activities.explanation: These words help you look closely and describe where things are.

tasks.then: Under means below, hidden beneath.

tasks.say: Throw the ball IN the basket.
tasks.then: In: the ball is inside the basket.

tasks.say: Now it is OUT of the basket.
tasks.then: Out: the ball is outside the basket.

activities.takeaway: Position words say where something is: above, on, under, near, in and out.
activities.explanation: Position words say where something is: above, on, under, near, in and out.

steps: The ball went into the basket, so it is inside.
The school word for inside is IN.

activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

lessons.title: Our National Flag

activities.prompt: What makes our national flag so special?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: Meet the Tiranga
activities.body: The National Flag is also called tiranga. Your book asks how many colours it has. It asks which colour is at the top, below white and above green. Another question asks where the ashoka chakra is. Children discuss when, where and why the flag is hoisted. They express feelings about National celebrations. They make their own tiranga and sing the National Anthem while standing and facing the tiranga.
keyPoints: The National Flag is also called tiranga.
Your book asks about colours and the ashoka chakra.
Children discuss hoisting, celebrations, making and singing.
activities.explanation: This card introduces the tiranga and the questions in your book.

They should stand and face the tiranga because that is how children sing.

how children can fold it safely

lessons.title: Chhuk Chhuk Goes Our Train

activities.prompt: What will our train see on its journey today?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: Our Train
activities.body: A train goes with a chhuk-chhuk sound. It goes over hills and down to the plains. It also goes over rivers and in the rain. Bogies make a chain. Some bogies come before another bogie, and some come after it. We can discuss what a train is and share our train journeys.
keyPoints: The train makes a chhuk-chhuk sound.
Bogies make a chain.
Some bogies come before or after another bogie.
activities.explanation: A train has many special parts, and each part helps us learn about it.

activities.prompt: Blue bogies are before red. Orange bogies are after it. What should the child colour?
steps: Find the red bogie in the chain, because both colour rules use it.
Colour the blue bogies before it, because blue must be coloured before red.
Colour the orange bogies after it, because orange must be coloured after red.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.
